title: US oil firm HKN aims to double output in Syria's formerly Kurdish-run fields
author: Amberin Zaman
text:
Interview

US oil firm HKN aims to double output in Syria's formerly Kurdish-run fields

HKN Vice President Matthew Zais tells Al-Monitor the company plans to double production at Syria’s northeastern oil fields while tackling pollution, as questions remain over the future of the Kurdish-run Jazira Oil Company.

Amberin Zaman

A general view shows the Awad oil field in the eastern Qamishli countryside in northeastern Syria, on Feb. 15, 2026. — Amjad Kurdo / Middle East Images / AFP via Getty Images

A Texas-based oil and gas company, HKN Energy, became the first US company to officially invest in Syria, signing a 25-year agreement in April with Syria’s state-run Syrian Petroleum Company (SPC) as first reported by Al-Monitor in June.HKN has started operations at eight fields around the town of Rmeilan in the Kurdish-administered part of northeast Syria. Those fields used to be run by the Jazira Oil Company, or JOC, which was taken over by the Kurds after the start of Syria’s civil conflict in 2011 and the Assad regime’s withdrawal from the area.HKN has partnered with Qatar’s UCC Holding but will be the sole operator of the fields.The company has a long record of doing business in the Kurdistan region of Iraq.
